anchors.description: 3D straight-line distance across the padded seat cushion of the nearer (left) striped terrace chair, from the cushion outer left end to its outer right end along the seat front edge.
anchors.visible_evidence: A row of identical slatted-wood terrace chairs with metal frames and blue/white striped seat pads stands along the wall benches. Both points sit on the cushion top face at its extreme left and right ends, so the chord spans the seat across its full width.
anchors.identity_uncertainty: Exact chair model is not identifiable. European bistro/terrace stacking chairs of this pattern have seat widths around 0.40-0.48 m. The chair is rotated a little relative to the camera, so the chord may pick up a small depth (diagonal) component, and the cushion corners are rounded, so the true span may differ by roughly 0.05-0.10 m.

anchors.description: 3D straight-line distance across the padded seat cushion of the second (right) terrace chair of the same model, from its cushion outer left end to its outer right end along the seat front edge.
anchors.visible_evidence: Same chair model as anchor a1 (identical wooden slat back and metal legs, same striped cushion) at the same table, seen a little closer to the camera. The two points lie at the extreme left and right ends of its cushion top face, so the chord measures the same seat-width dimension.
anchors.identity_uncertainty: Same class prior as a1: seat width assumed 0.40-0.48 m. This chair is turned at a different yaw from the left chair, so the chord has a different depth component and the two estimates are only approximately consistent.
